chapters.title: Egypt Is Man, Not God
chapters.html:
Isaiah 31

1Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help,
who rely on horses,
who trust in chariots because they are many,
and in horsemen because they are very strong,
but do not look to the Holy One of Israel
or seek the LORD!

2Yet He too is wise, and brings disaster;
He does not take back His words;
He will rise against the house of evildoers,
and against the helpers of those who work iniquity.

3The Egyptians are man, and not God;
their horses are flesh, and not spirit.
When the LORD stretches out His hand,
the helper will stumble, and the one helped will fall,
and they will all perish together.

4For thus the LORD said to me:
"As a lion or a young lion growls over its prey,
and when a band of shepherds is called out against it,
it is not terrified by their shouting
or daunted by their noise,
so the LORD of hosts will come down
to fight upon Mount Zion and upon its hill.

5Like birds hovering,
so the LORD of hosts will shield Jerusalem;
He will shield and rescue it;
He will pass over and deliver it."

6Return to Him from whom the sons of Israel have so deeply turned away.

7For in that day each of you will reject his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which your hands have made for you in sin.

8"Assyria will fall by a sword, not of man,
and a sword, not of a human, will devour him;
he will flee from the sword,
and his young men will be put to forced labor.

9His rock will pass away in terror,
and his commanders will be dismayed at the signal,"
declares the LORD,
whose fire is in Zion,
and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

Notes

  • v1 "who go down to Egypt… who rely on horses" — the law forbade the king to multiply horses for himself or to make the people return to Egypt to get them (Deuteronomy 17:16). The note on 2:7 counts the horses among the three things forbidden.

  • v3 "The Egyptians are man, and not God; their horses are flesh, and not spirit" — adam against El, basar against ruach: flesh is what man is, and spirit what God gives and takes back (My breath shall not remain in the human forever, in that he also is flesh, Genesis 6:3).

  • v4 "to fight upon Mount Zion" — litsbo al. In 29:7–8 the same words are used of the nations that fight against Mount Zion, and al can be "against" as well as "upon." Here v5 settles which: the LORD comes down as the lion that will not give up its prey, to shield the city, not to take it.

  • v5 "He will shield and rescue it; He will pass over and deliver it" — pasoach, the verb of the Passover, and hitsil, "rescue," the two verbs of Exodus 12:27, the LORD, who passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck Egypt, and He rescued our houses. Jerusalem is spared as Israel's houses were.

  • v8 "a sword, not of man" — the city is delivered by no army; Isaiah tells the night it happened: The messenger of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians (37:36).

  • v9 "whose fire is in Zion, and whose furnace is in Jerusalem" — the altar fire of Ariel, the hearth-city of 29:1–2, here a furnace for the enemy.

chapters.title: A King Will Reign in Righteousness
chapters.html:
Isaiah 32

1A king will reign in righteousness,
and princes will rule in justice.

2Each will be like a hiding place from the wind,
a shelter from the storm,
like streams of water in a dry place,
like the shade of a great rock in a weary land.

3Then the eyes of those who see will not be closed,
and the ears of those who hear will listen.

4The heart of the rash will understand and know,
and the tongue of the stammerers will hasten to speak clearly.

5The fool will no longer be called noble,
nor the scoundrel be said to be generous.

6For the fool speaks folly,
and his heart plans iniquity:
to practice ungodliness,
to speak error concerning the LORD,
to leave the hungry empty,
and to deprive the thirsty of drink.

7As for the scoundrel, his schemes are evil;
he devises wicked plans
to ruin the poor with lying words,
even when the plea of the needy is right.

8But the noble plans noble things,
and on noble things he stands.

The Women at Ease

9Women at ease, rise up, hear my voice;
complacent daughters, give ear to my speech.

10In little more than a year
you will shudder, you complacent ones;
for the vintage will fail;
the harvest will not come.

11Tremble, you women at ease;
shudder, you complacent ones;
strip and make yourselves bare,
and put sackcloth on your waist.

12Beat your breasts
for the pleasant fields,
for the fruitful vine,

13for the soil of my people
growing up in thorns and briers,
yes, for all the joyful houses
in the exultant city.

14For the palace is forsaken,
the crowded city deserted;
the Ophel and the watchtower
will be dens forever,
a joy of wild donkeys,
a pasture for flocks;

15until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high,
and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field,
and the fruitful field is regarded as a forest.

16Then justice will dwell in the wilderness,
and righteousness abide in the fruitful field.

17The work of righteousness will be peace,
and the result of righteousness, quietness and trust forever.

18My people will dwell in a peaceful home,
in secure dwellings,
and in resting places at ease.

19But hail will fall when the forest comes down,
and the city will be brought low, utterly low.

20Blessed are you who sow beside all waters,
who let the ox and the donkey range free.

Notes

  • v3 "the eyes of those who see will not be closed" — lo tish'enah, the verb of Isaiah's commission, shut their eyes (6:10, hasha). What was closed then is opened.

  • vv5–6 "The fool… the fool speaks folly" — naval, the word that was a man's name: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him (1 Samuel 25:25). Naval nevalah yedabber, "the fool speaks folly," turns the noun into its own verb's object.

  • v7 "the scoundrel, his schemes" — kelai kelav, the scoundrel and his tools, two words that sound alike. The read form aniyyim, "the poor," is followed.

  • vv9, 11, 18 "Women at ease… in resting places at ease" — sha'anannot, "at ease," twice of the women whose ease is false, and once more in v18 of the people's true rest, menuchot sha'anannot: the same word, the false ease taken away and the true one given.

  • v12 "Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields" — al shadayim… al sedei chemed, "breasts" and "fields," two words that sound alike.

  • v15 "until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high" — ruach mi-marom, the LORD's Spirit, as in 44:3, I will pour My Spirit on your seed. Then the reversal of 29:17: wilderness to fruitful field, fruitful field to forest.

  • v17 "quietness and trust" — hashqet va-vetach, the words of 30:15, in quietness and trust will be your strength, which the people refused. Here it is the fruit of righteousness.

chapters.title: Who Can Live with the Devouring Fire?
chapters.html:
Isaiah 33

1Woe to you, destroyer,
who yourself have not been destroyed,
you traitor,
whom no one has betrayed!
When you have finished destroying,
you will be destroyed;
when you have done betraying,
they will betray you.

2LORD, be gracious to us;
we wait for You.
Be their arm every morning,
our deliverance in the time of trouble.

3At the sound of the tumult peoples flee;
when You rise up, nations scatter;

4and your spoil is gathered as the caterpillar gathers;
as locusts leap, men leap on it.

5The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high;
He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness;

6There will be stability in your times,
a wealth of deliverance, wisdom and knowledge;
the fear of the LORD is his treasure.

7Their valiant ones cry out in the streets;
the envoys of peace weep bitterly.

8The highways lie waste;
the traveler has ceased.
He has broken the covenant;
he has despised the cities;
he has no regard for man.

9The land mourns and languishes;
Lebanon is ashamed and withers;
Sharon is like a desert;
Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.

10"Now I will arise," says the LORD,
"now I will rise high;
now I will be lifted up.

11You conceive chaff;
you give birth to stubble;
your breath is a fire that will consume you.

12The peoples will be as if burned to lime,
like thorns cut down that are burned in the fire.

13Hear, you who are far off, what I have done;
and you who are near, acknowledge My might."

14The sinners in Zion are afraid;
trembling has seized the godless:
"Who among us can live as a guest with the devouring fire?
Who among us can live as a guest with everlasting burnings?"

15He who walks righteously and speaks uprightly,
who rejects the gain of oppression,
who shakes his hands free of a bribe,
who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed,
and shuts his eyes from looking on evil,

16he will dwell on the heights;
his refuge will be the fortresses of rocks;
his bread will be given him;
his water will be sure.

17Your eyes will see the King in His beauty;
they will see a land that stretches afar.

18Your heart will muse on the terror:
"Where is he who counted?
Where is he who weighed the tribute?
Where is he who counted the towers?"

19You will no longer see the insolent people,
the people of a speech too deep to understand,
of a stammering tongue that no one comprehends.

20Look on Zion, the city of our appointed feasts!
Your eyes will see Jerusalem,
a home at ease, a tent that will not be moved,
whose stakes will never be pulled up,
nor any of its cords be broken.

21But there the LORD in majesty will be for us
a place of broad rivers and streams,
where no galley with oars can go,
nor majestic ship pass.

22For the LORD is our judge;
the LORD is our lawgiver;
the LORD is our king;
He will save us.

23Your ropes hang loose;
they cannot hold the mast firm in its place
or keep the sail spread.
Then prey and spoil in abundance will be divided;
even the lame will take the plunder.

24No inhabitant will say, "I am sick";
the people who dwell there will be forgiven their iniquity.

Notes

  • v1 "Woe to you, destroyer… traitor" — shoded and boged, the pair of 21:2 and 24:16, the traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. Here the destroyer is told it will be done to him.

  • v2 "Be their arm every morning, our deliverance" — zero'am, "their arm," the prayer turning from us to them and back in one line. The Greek has another line entirely.

  • v6 "wisdom and knowledge; the fear of the LORD" — the gifts of the Spirit on the shoot of Jesse in 11:2. Otsaro, "his treasure," names no one; the nearest are Zion and the LORD in v5.

  • v7 "Their valiant ones" — er'ellam, a word found only here, and close to Ariel (29:1); "valiant ones" is the sense the parallel envoys of peace allows.

  • v10 "now I will rise high; now I will be lifted up" — eromam… ennase, from rum and nasa, the words of the throne in 6:1, high and lifted up, and of the servant in 52:13, he will be high and lifted up.

  • vv14–16 "Who among us can live as a guest with the devouring fire?… He who walks righteously" — mi yagur, the question of Psalm 15:1, LORD, who shall live as a guest in Your tent?, answered the same way: The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right (15:2). Here the LORD's presence is a fire, and only the righteous can live in it.

  • vv17, 22 "Your eyes will see the King in His beauty… the LORD is our king" — the king of v17 is not named; v22 names the LORD as king, and Isaiah's own cry in the temple was my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts (6:5). "Lawgiver" — mechoqeq, the staff of Genesis 49:10.

  • v18 "Where is he who counted?" — the Assyrian officials who counted the tribute and the towers are gone. The Greek has Where are the scribes?, and Paul's questions follow it: Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? (1 Corinthians 1:20).

  • v19 "a stammering tongue" — nil'ag lashon, the foreign speech of 28:11, with stammering lips and another tongue.

  • v23 "even the lame will take the plunder" — bazezu baz, the plunder of Maher-shalal-hash-baz (8:1), now taken by the weakest.

chapters.title: The Day of Vengeance on Edom
chapters.html:
Isaiah 34

1Draw near, you nations, to hear;
and listen, you peoples!
Let the earth hear, and all that fills it;
the world, and all that comes from it.

2For the LORD is enraged against all the nations,
and furious against all their host;
He has devoted them to destruction,
He has given them over for slaughter.

3Their slain will be cast out,
and the stench of their corpses will rise;
the mountains will melt with their blood.

4All the host of heaven will rot away,
and the skies roll up like a scroll;
all their host will wither
as a leaf withers from the vine,
like a withered fig from the fig tree.

5For My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens;
it descends on Edom,
on the people I have devoted to destruction, for judgment.

6The LORD has a sword; it is full of blood;
it is gorged with fat,
with the blood of lambs and goats,
with the fat of the kidneys of rams.
For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah,
a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

7Wild oxen will fall with them,
and young bulls with the mighty bulls.
Their land will drink its fill of blood,
and their dust will be gorged with fat.

8For the LORD has a day of vengeance,
a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.

9Edom's streams will be turned into pitch,
and its dust into sulfur;
its land will become burning pitch.

10Night and day it will not be quenched;
its smoke will go up forever.
From generation to generation it will lie waste;
none will pass through it forever and ever.

11The pelican and the hedgehog will possess it;
the great owl and the raven will dwell in it.
He will stretch over it the line of the wild
and the stones of the waste.

12Its nobles — there is no one there to call it a kingdom,
and all its princes will be nothing.

13Thorns will grow over its palaces,
nettles and thistles in its fortresses;
it will be a haunt of jackals,
an abode for ostriches.

14Wild beasts will meet with hyenas;
the goat-spirit will cry to his fellow;
there too Lilith will settle
and find herself a place of rest.

15There the owl will nest and lay her eggs,
and hatch them and gather her young in her shadow;
there too the kites will gather,
each one with her mate.

16Seek in the book of the LORD, and read:
not one of these will be missing;
none will lack her mate.
For My mouth has commanded,
and His Spirit has gathered them.

17He has cast the lot for them;
His hand has portioned it out to them by the line;
they will possess it forever;
from generation to generation they will dwell in it.

Notes

  • vv2, 5 "He has devoted them to destruction… the people I have devoted to destruction" — hecherim, cheremi: the ban that was laid on the cities of Canaan (11:15 note; Joshua 6:21) is laid on the nations, and on Edom by name.

  • v4 "the skies roll up like a scroll… as a leaf withers… like a withered fig from the fig tree" — Revelation takes up both pictures: the stars of heaven fell to the earth as a fig tree drops its unripe figs… and the sky was split apart like a scroll being rolled up (Revelation 6:13–14).

  • vv6–7 "a sacrifice in Bozrah" — Edom's city, from which the LORD is seen coming in 63:1, in crimsoned garments from Bozrah. The slaughter is described as an offering: the blood and fat of lambs, goats and rams that the law gave to the altar.

  • v8 "a day of vengeance, a year of recompense" — the pair returns in 61:2, the year of the LORD's favor, and the day of vengeance of our God.

  • vv9–10 "pitch… sulfur… its smoke will go up forever" — the overthrow of Sodom, where Abraham saw the smoke of the land going up like the smoke of a kiln (Genesis 19:28). Revelation says the same of Babylon: her smoke goes up forever and ever (Revelation 19:3).

  • v11 "the line of the wild and the stones of the waste" — qav tohu ve-avnei vohu, the tohu va-vohu of Genesis 1:2, wild and waste, split across a builder's tools: the measuring line (qav, 28:17) and the plumb stones are used to unmake. "The pelican" — qa'at, the bird of Leviticus 11:18. "The hedgehog" — qippod, as in 14:23.

  • v14 "the goat-spirit… Lilith" — sa'ir, as in 13:21; lilit, a word found only here, built like layil, "night." Read as a name, it is Lilith, a creature of the night; the Greek has onokentauroi, "donkey-centaurs." The wild things settle where Edom's kings were.

  • v16 "For My mouth has commanded" — ki fi hu tsivvah, "for my mouth, it has commanded." The mouth is the LORD's (the line goes on and His Spirit has gathered them) or the prophet's, who has just told the reader to seek in the book of the LORD; the Hebrew does not say which. The Greek reads the Lord commanded them.

  • vv16–17 "Seek in the book of the LORD… He has cast the lot for them… by the line" — goral and qav: the land is shared out to the owls and jackals by lot and measuring line, as Canaan was shared out to the tribes (Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the LORD, Joshua 18:10).

Seek in the book of the LORD, and read: not one of these will be missing; none will lack her mate. For My mouth has commanded, and His Spirit has gathered them.

chapters.title: The Way of Holiness
chapters.html:
Isaiah 35

1The wilderness and the dry land will be glad;
the desert will rejoice and blossom;
like the flower

2it will blossom abundantly,
and rejoice with joy and singing.
The glory of Lebanon will be given to it,
the splendor of Carmel and Sharon.
They will see the glory of the LORD,
the splendor of our God.

3Strengthen the weak hands,
and make firm the feeble knees.

4Say to those whose hearts are anxious,
"Be strong; do not fear!
Here is your God! He will come with vengeance,
with the recompense of God.
He will come and save you."

5Then the eyes of the blind will be opened,
and the ears of the deaf unstopped;

6then the lame will leap like a deer,
and the tongue of the mute sing for joy.
For waters will break out in the wilderness,
and streams in the desert;

7the burning sand will become a pool,
and the thirsty ground springs of water;
in the haunt of jackals, where they lay,
grass will become reeds and rushes.

8A highway will be there, a road,
and it will be called the Way of Holiness;
the unclean will not pass over it.
It will be for those who walk the way;
fools will not wander on it.

9No lion will be there,
nor will any ravenous beast go up on it;
they will not be found there;
but the redeemed will walk there.

10The ransomed of the LORD will return
and come to Zion with singing;
everlasting joy will be on their heads;
they will obtain gladness and joy,
and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "like the flower… the splendor of Carmel and Sharon" — chavatselet, the flower of I am a flower of Sharon (Song of Songs 2:1); here too Sharon is named. In 33:9 Lebanon is ashamed and withers; Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves; here the same three places are given back.

  • v3 "Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees" — the letter to the Hebrews quotes it to people worn out by discipline: lift your drooping hands and strengthen your weak knees (Hebrews 12:12).

  • v4 "Here is your God!… He will come and save you" — hinneh Eloheikhem, the words the herald is told to cry to the towns of Judah in 40:9. Save is yasha, the root of yeshu'ah, "deliverance" (12:2–3).

  • vv5–6 "the eyes of the blind will be opened… the lame will leap" — the signs Jesus names to John's disciples: the blind see again and the lame walk… and the deaf hear (Matthew 11:5). The eyes and ears shut in 6:10 are opened.

  • v8 "the Way of Holiness" — derekh ha-qodesh, the highway of 11:16 and 19:23, now named. Only the clean walk it, and it is so plain that fools will not wander on it.

  • vv9–10 "the redeemed… the ransomed of the LORD" — ge'ulim, from ga'al, the next of kin who buys back, and peduyim, from padah, "ransom." Verse 10 stands again, almost word for word, at 51:11.

chapters.title: The Rabshakeh at the Wall
chapters.html:
Isaiah 36

1And it came to pass in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.

2The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a great army. He stood by the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field.

3Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came out to him.

The Rabshakeh's Speech

4The Rabshakeh said to them, "Say to Hezekiah, 'Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence in which you trust?

5I say that counsel and strength for war are only a word of the lips. Now, in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?

6You are trusting in the staff of this crushed reed, in Egypt, which will pierce the hand of any man who leans on it and go into it. Such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

7But if you say to me, "We trust in the LORD our God," is it not He whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and to Jerusalem, "You shall bow down before this altar"?'

8So now, make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to put riders on them.

9How then can you turn back a single governor among the least of my master's servants, when you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?

10Now, have I come up against this land to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"

11Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people who are on the wall."

12But the Rabshakeh said, "Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you, and not to the men sitting on the wall, who are doomed with you to eat their own excrement and drink their own urine?"

13Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in the language of Judah, and said, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!

14Thus says the king: 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you.

15Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD, saying, "The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."

16Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: Make peace with me and come out to me, and each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and each will drink the water of his own cistern,

17until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.

18Do not let Hezekiah mislead you, saying, "The LORD will deliver us." Has any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

19Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?

20Who among all the gods of these lands have delivered their land out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?'"

21But they were silent and did not answer him a word, for the king's command was, "Do not answer him."

22Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him the words of the Rabshakeh.

Notes

  • vv1–22 and 2 Kings 18 — the same account stands in 2 Kings 18:13–37, nearly word for word. Isaiah lacks the tribute Hezekiah paid from the temple's gold (2 Kings 18:14–16), sends only the Rabshakeh where Kings names three officers, and leaves out a land of olive oil and honey, so that you may live and not die (v17) and the towns Hena and Ivvah (v19).

  • v2 "the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Launderer's Field" — the place where Isaiah was sent to meet Ahaz and tell him not to fear (7:3). The king who would not trust is gone; at the same spot his son's envoys hear Assyria mock their trust.

  • v5 "I say that counsel and strength for war are only a word of the lips" — amarti, "I say." Kings has amarta, "you say": there the Rabshakeh quotes Hezekiah; here he gives his own verdict.

  • v6 "this crushed reed, in Egypt" — the same judgment Isaiah had given: Egypt's help is vapor and emptiness (30:7); Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help (31:1).

  • v10 "The LORD said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it'" — the boast is half true. The LORD had sent Assyria: Against a godless nation I send him (10:6). He had also said what happens when the rod forgets whose hand holds it (10:12–15).

  • vv11–13 "Aramaic… the language of Judah" — aramit, the speech of diplomats, and yehudit, "Judean," the people's own Hebrew. The officials ask for the language the people on the wall cannot follow; the Rabshakeh answers in the one they can.

  • v16 "each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree" — the picture of peace in Solomon's days, each man under his vine and under his fig tree (1 Kings 4:25), offered as the price of surrender.

  • vv18–20 "Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad?" — the boast Isaiah put in the king's mouth in 10:9–11: Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?

chapters.title: Hezekiah's Prayer and the Night of the Messenger
chapters.html:
Isaiah 37

Hezekiah Sends to Isaiah

1And it came to pass, when King Hezekiah heard it, that he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.

2He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the secretary and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz.

3They said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: 'This day is a day of distress, of rebuke and of disgrace. The children have come to the mouth of the womb, and there is no strength to give birth.

4It may be that the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. So lift up a prayer for the remnant that is left.'"

5So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,

6and Isaiah said to them, "Say this to your master: 'Thus says the LORD: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have reviled Me.

7I will put a spirit in him, so that he will hear a report and return to his own land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.'"

Sennacherib's Letter

8The Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.

9Then the king heard it said of Tirhakah king of Cush, "He has come out to fight against you." When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

10"Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: 'Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you by saying, "Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."

11You have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. Will you be delivered?

12Did the gods of the nations deliver them, the nations my fathers destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?

13Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena and Ivvah?'"

Hezekiah's Prayer

14Hezekiah took the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.

15Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, saying,

16"O LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, who is enthroned on the cherubim, You are God, You alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made the heavens and the earth.

17Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see. Hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to defy the living God.

18Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the lands and their land,

19and have cast their gods into the fire, for they were no gods, but the work of human hands, wood and stone; so they destroyed them.

20So now, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone are the LORD."

The Word of the LORD against Sennacherib

21Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,

22this is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him:
She despises you, she scorns you,
the virgin daughter of Zion;
behind you she shakes her head,
the daughter of Jerusalem.

23Whom have you defied and reviled?
Against whom have you raised your voice
and lifted your eyes on high?
Against the Holy One of Israel!

24By your servants you have defied the Lord,
and you have said, 'With the multitude of my chariots
I have gone up to the heights of the mountains,
to the far reaches of Lebanon.
I cut down its tallest cedars,
its choicest cypresses;
I entered its farthest height,
its densest forest.

25I dug wells and drank waters,
and with the sole of my feet I dried up
all the streams of Egypt.'

26Have you not heard?
Long ago I made it;
from days of old I formed it;
now I have brought it to pass,
that you should turn fortified cities
into heaps of ruins,

27while their inhabitants, short of strength,
were dismayed and put to shame.
They were like the grass of the field
and the green herb,
like grass on the housetops,
like a field before the grain has grown.

28I know your sitting down,
your going out and your coming in,
and your raging against Me.

29Because you have raged against Me
and your arrogance has come up to My ears,
I will put My hook in your nose
and My bit in your lips,
and I will turn you back on the way
by which you came.

30"This shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that; then in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

31The survivors of the house of Judah who remain shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.

32For out of Jerusalem shall go a remnant, and survivors out of Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this.

33"Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city or shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with a shield, nor cast up a siege mound against it.

34By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and he shall not come into this city, declares the LORD.

35For I will defend this city to save it, for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant."

The Night of the Messenger

36The messenger of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. When people rose early in the morning, they were all dead bodies.

37So Sennacherib king of Assyria set out and went home, and lived in Nineveh.

38As he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–38 and 2 Kings 19 — the same account, nearly word for word. Isaiah numbers it one verse longer, dividing Hezekiah's prayer after saying (vv15–16). The differences: the LORD of hosts in the prayer (v16); that You alone are the LORD where Kings has that You, O LORD, are God alone (v20); no I have heard after the prayer, so that the answer runs straight on, Because you have prayed to Me… this is the word (vv21–22); by your servants for Kings' by your messengers (v24); waters where Kings has foreign waters (v25); a field (shedemah) where Kings has scorched (shedefah) (v27); and no And it came to pass that night (v36).

  • v3 "The children have come to the mouth of the womb, and there is no strength to give birth" — the picture of 26:18, we were with child; we writhed; we gave birth, as it were, to wind.

  • vv4, 31–32 "a prayer for the remnant… a remnant, and survivors out of Mount Zion" — she'erit and peletah, the words of 10:20, the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob.

  • vv26–29 "Long ago I made it… I will put My hook in your nose" — the answer of 10:5–15: Assyria was the rod in the LORD's hand, and the rod boasted. "Your raging against Me" — hitraggezkha, from ragaz, "to tremble, rage."

  • v31 "take root downward and bear fruit upward" — as in 27:6, Jacob will take root; Israel will blossom and put out shoots.

  • v32 "The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this" — the words that close the promise of the child on David's throne (9:7).

  • v36 "The messenger of the LORD went out" — what 10:33–34 and 31:8 had announced: Assyria will fall by a sword, not of man. Mal'akh, "messenger," the word for the LORD's sent one.

  • vv37–38 "in the house of Nisroch his god… his sons struck him down" — the king who asked Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? (36:19) dies in the house of his own god.

chapters.title: Hezekiah's Sickness and His Song
chapters.html:
Isaiah 38

1In those days Hezekiah became sick and was near death. Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz came to him and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Set your house in order, for you shall die; you shall not live.'"

2Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,

3and said, "Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes." Hezekiah wept bitterly.

4Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,

5"Go and say to Hezekiah, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. I will add fifteen years to your days.

6I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.

7This is the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that He has spoken:

8I am about to make the shadow on the steps, which has gone down on the steps of Ahaz with the sun, go back ten steps.'" So the sun went back ten steps on the steps by which it had gone down.

Hezekiah's Song

9A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick and had recovered from his sickness:

10I said: In the quiet of my days
I must go to the gates of Sheol;
I am deprived of the rest of my years.

11I said: I will not see Yah,
Yah in the land of the living;
I will look on man no more
among those who dwell where all has ceased.

12My dwelling is pulled up and taken from me
like a shepherd's tent;
I have rolled up my life like a weaver;
He cuts me off from the loom;
from day to night You bring me to an end.

13I quieted myself until morning;
like a lion He breaks all my bones;
from day to night You bring me to an end.

14Like a swift, like a crane, I chirp;
I moan like a dove;
my eyes are worn out with looking upward.
Lord, I am oppressed; be my pledge!

15What shall I say?
He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done it.
I will walk slowly all my years
because of the bitterness of my soul.

16Lord, by these things men live,
and in all of them is the life of my spirit;
You restore me to health and make me live.

17It was for my peace
that I had bitter, bitter grief;
but You have set Your heart on my soul
and kept it from the pit of destruction,
for You have cast all my sins
behind Your back.

18For Sheol does not thank You;
death does not praise You;
those who go down to the pit
do not hope for Your faithfulness.

19The living, the living, he thanks You,
as I do this day;
a father makes known to his children
Your faithfulness.

20The LORD is ready to save me,
and we will play my songs on strings
all the days of our life,
at the house of the LORD.

  • vv1–8, 21–22 and 2 Kings 20 — the account of 2 Kings 20:1–11, shortened, with Hezekiah's song in the middle.   • v9 "A writing of Hezekiah" — mikhtav, "a writing"; the Psalms' heading mikhtam (Psalm 16) differs by one letter.

and said, "Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes." Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,
"Go and say to Hezekiah, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. I will add fifteen years to your days.

Hezekiah said, "What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?"

chapters.title: The Envoys from Babylon
chapters.html:
Isaiah 39

1At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that he had been sick and had recovered.

2Hezekiah was glad of them, and he showed them his treasure house, the silver, the gold, the spices and the fine oil, all his armory and all that was found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.

3Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say? From where did they come to you?" Hezekiah said, "They have come to me from a far country, from Babylon."

4He said, "What have they seen in your house?" Hezekiah answered, "They have seen all that is in my house. There is nothing in my treasuries that I did not show them."

5Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD of hosts:

6The days are coming when all that is in your house, and what your fathers have stored up until this day, shall be carried to Babylon. Nothing shall be left, says the LORD.

7Some of your sons, who will come from you, whom you will father, shall be taken away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon."

8Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." For he said, "There will be peace and security in my days."

Notes

  • vv1–8 and 2 Kings 20 — the account of 2 Kings 20:12–19, nearly word for word. Isaiah has he had been sick and had recovered (v1), They have come to me (v3), the word of the LORD of hosts (v5), and in v8 Hezekiah's thought stated flat, There will be peace and security in my days, where Kings has it as a question, Is it not so, if there will be peace and security in my days?

  • v1 "Merodach-baladan" — Kings spells the name Berodach. The king of the city whose fall Isaiah has already sung (13:1; 21:9) comes first as a friend with a gift.

  • v6 "shall be carried to Babylon" — the first time Isaiah names Babylon as the place of exile. The next chapter opens on the far side of it: Comfort, comfort My people (40:1).

  • v7 "they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon" — Daniel's story begins there: the king tells Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring some of the sons of Israel, of the royal family and of the nobles (Daniel 1:3).

  • v8 "There will be peace and security in my days" — shalom ve-emet. The king who wept for fifteen more years (38:3, 5) takes the word of loss with relief that it will not fall in his time.

chapters.title: Comfort, Comfort My People
chapters.html:
Isaiah 40

1Comfort, comfort My people,
says your God.

2Speak to the heart of Jerusalem,
and call out to her
that her hard service is ended,
that her iniquity is paid for,
that she has received from the LORD's hand
double for all her sins.

3A voice calls:
"In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD;
make straight in the desert
a highway for our God.

4Every valley shall be lifted up,
and every mountain and hill made low;
the uneven ground shall become level,
and the rough places a plain.

5The glory of the LORD shall be revealed,
and all flesh shall see it together,
for the mouth of the LORD has spoken."

6A voice says, "Call out!"
and one says, "What shall I call out?"
All flesh is grass,
and all its loyalty is like the flower of the field.

7The grass withers, the flower fades,
when the Spirit of the LORD blows on it;
surely the people are grass.

8The grass withers, the flower fades,
but the word of our God will stand forever.

9Go up on a high mountain,
Zion, herald of good news;
lift up your voice with strength,
Jerusalem, herald of good news;
lift it up, do not fear;
say to the cities of Judah,
"Here is your God!"

10Here is the Lord GOD! He comes with might,
and His arm rules for Him;
His reward is with Him,
and His recompense before Him.

11He will tend His flock like a shepherd;
He will gather the lambs in His arm
and carry them in His bosom,
and gently lead those that are nursing.

To Whom Will You Liken God?

12Who has measured the waters in the hollow of His hand,
and marked off the heavens with a span,
and held the dust of the earth in a measure,
and weighed the mountains in scales
and the hills in a balance?

13Who has marked out the Spirit of the LORD,
or what man has shown Him His counsel?

14Whom did He consult, and who made Him understand?
Who taught Him the path of justice,
and taught Him knowledge,
and showed Him the way of understanding?

15The nations are like a drop from a bucket,
and are counted as dust on the scales;
He lifts up the coastlands like fine dust.

16Lebanon is not enough for fuel,
nor its beasts enough for a burnt offering.

17All the nations are as nothing before Him;
they are counted by Him as less than nothing and emptiness.

18To whom then will you liken God,
or what likeness will you set beside Him?

19An idol! A craftsman casts it,
and a goldsmith overlays it with gold
and casts silver chains for it.

20He who is too poor for such an offering
chooses wood that will not rot;
he seeks out a skilled craftsman
to set up an idol that will not totter.

21Do you not know? Do you not hear?
Has it not been told you from the beginning?
Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?

22It is He who sits above the circle of the earth,
and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers;
who stretches out the heavens like a curtain,
and spreads them like a tent to dwell in;

23who brings princes to nothing,
and makes the rulers of the earth as emptiness.

24Scarcely are they planted,
scarcely sown,
scarcely has their stump taken root in the earth,
when He blows on them and they wither,
and the storm carries them off like stubble.

25"To whom then will you liken Me,
that I should be equal?" says the Holy One.

26Lift up your eyes on high and see:
who created these?
He who brings out their host by number,
calling them all by name;
by the greatness of His might,
and because He is strong in power,
not one is missing.

27Why do you say, Jacob,
and speak, Israel,
"My way is hidden from the LORD,
and my right is passed over by my God"?

28Have you not known? Have you not heard?
The LORD is the everlasting God,
the Creator of the ends of the earth.
He does not grow faint or weary;
His understanding is unsearchable.

29He gives power to the faint,
and to him who has no might He increases strength.

30Even youths grow faint and weary,
and young men stumble and fall;

31but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength;
they will mount up with wings like eagles;
they will run and not grow weary;
they will walk and not grow faint.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Comfort, comfort… Speak to the heart of Jerusalem" — nachamu and dabberu al lev, the two verbs of Joseph with his frightened brothers: He comforted them and spoke to their heart (Genesis 50:21). After 39:6–7, carried to Babylon, the book's second half opens on the other side of the exile.

  • v2 "her iniquity is paid for" — nirtsah avonah, the verb of the law's promise to a people in exile, they pay for their guilt (Leviticus 26:41). "Her hard service" — tseva'ah, the word for a soldier's term of duty.

  • v3 "A voice calls: 'In the wilderness prepare the way'" — in the Hebrew in the wilderness belongs to the road, matched by in the desert. The Greek reads A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way, and the Gospels quote it so of John the Baptist (A voice of one crying out in the wilderness: "Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight," Matthew 3:3; John 1:23).

  • vv6–8 "all its loyalty is like the flower of the field… the word of our God will stand forever" — chasdo, "its chesed," the word for loyal love, in man as frail as a wildflower. The Greek has all the glory of man, and Peter quotes it: all its glory like the flower of grass… but the word of the Lord remains forever (1 Peter 1:24–25).

  • vv7, 13 "the Spirit of the LORD blows on it… Who has marked out the Spirit of the LORD?" — ruach YHWH both times: the wind that withers the grass, and the Spirit no one can measure. The Greek reads v13 Who has known the mind of the Lord?, and Paul quotes that (Romans 11:34).

  • v9 "Zion, herald of good news" — mevaseret Tsiyyon, a feminine noun, and the city itself is the herald. The Greek reads it you who bring good news to Zion with the verb euangelizesthai, from which gospel comes. Here is your God (hinneh Eloheikhem) is the cry of 35:4.

  • vv10–11 "His reward is with Him… He will tend His flock like a shepherd… gently lead" — yenahel, the verb of He leads me beside still waters (Psalm 23:2). Revelation takes up the first line: My reward is with Me (Revelation 22:12).

  • v18 "what likeness will you set beside Him?" — demut, the word of Let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness (Genesis 1:26). Man was made in God's likeness; nothing made can be set up as His.

  • vv20, 24 "an idol that will not totter… scarcely has their stump taken root" — the idol is fixed so that it will not totter (lo yimmot), as in 41:7. Giz'am, "their stump," is the geza of 11:1, a shoot from the stump of Jesse: the rulers' stump never roots.

  • vv28–31 "He does not grow faint or weary… they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not grow faint" — ya'af and yaga, the same two verbs four times: what the LORD never does (v28), what even the young do (v30), and what those who wait for Him will not do (v31).

chapters.title: Do Not Fear, I Am with You
chapters.html:
Isaiah 41

1Be silent before Me, coastlands;
let the peoples renew their strength;
let them approach, then let them speak;
let us come together for judgment.

2Who has stirred up one from the east,
whom righteousness calls to its feet?
He gives up nations before him
and makes him trample kings;
he makes them like dust with his sword,
like driven stubble with his bow.

3He pursues them and passes on in safety,
by a path his feet have not trodden.

4Who has done this and carried it out,
calling the generations from the beginning?
I, the LORD, the first,
and with the last, I am He.

5The coastlands have seen and are afraid;
the ends of the earth tremble;
they have drawn near and come.

6Each one helps his neighbor,
and says to his brother, "Be strong!"

7The craftsman encourages the goldsmith,
and he who smooths with the hammer
him who strikes the anvil,
saying of the soldering, "It is good";
and he fastens it with nails so that it will not totter.

8But you, Israel, My servant,
Jacob, whom I have chosen,
the offspring of Abraham, My friend,

9you whom I took hold of from the ends of the earth,
and called from its farthest corners,
saying to you, "You are My servant;
I have chosen you and not rejected you";

10do not fear, for I am with you;
do not be dismayed, for I am your God;
I will strengthen you, I will help you;
I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.

11All who are incensed against you
will be put to shame and disgraced;
those who strive with you
will be as nothing and perish.

12You will seek those who contend with you,
but you will not find them;
those who war against you
will be as nothing at all.

13For I, the LORD your God,
hold your right hand;
it is I who say to you, "Do not fear;
I will help you."

14Do not fear, you worm Jacob,
you men of Israel!
I will help you, declares the LORD;
your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.

15I will make you a threshing sledge,
new, sharp, with many teeth;
you will thresh the mountains and crush them,
and make the hills like chaff.

16You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away,
and the storm will scatter them;
but you will rejoice in the LORD;
in the Holy One of Israel you will glory.

17The poor and needy seek water, and there is none;
their tongue is parched with thirst;
I, the LORD, will answer them;
I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.

18I will open rivers on the bare heights,
and springs in the middle of the valleys;
I will make the wilderness a pool of water,
and the dry land springs of water.

19I will put in the wilderness the cedar,
the acacia, the myrtle and the olive;
I will set in the desert the cypress,
the plane and the pine together,

20that they may see and know,
may consider and understand together,
that the hand of the LORD has done this,
the Holy One of Israel has created it.

The Idols on Trial

21Set forth your case, says the LORD;
bring your strong arguments, says the King of Jacob.

22Let them bring them and tell us
what is to happen.
Tell us the former things, what they were,
that we may consider them
and know their outcome;
or declare to us the things to come.

23Tell us what is to come hereafter,
that we may know that you are gods;
do good, or do harm,
that we may be dismayed and see it together.

24You are less than nothing,
and your work is less than nothing;
whoever chooses you is detestable.

25I have stirred up one from the north, and he has come,
from the rising of the sun, one who calls on My name;
he will come on rulers as on mortar,
as the potter treads clay.

26Who declared it from the beginning, that we might know,
and beforehand, that we might say, "He is right"?
There was no one who declared it,
no one who proclaimed it,
no one who heard your words.

27I first said to Zion, "Here they are!"
and I give Jerusalem a herald of good news.

28But when I look, there is no one;
among these there is no counselor
who, when I ask, gives an answer.

29They are all a delusion;
their works are nothing;
their metal images are wind and emptiness.

Notes

  • v1 "let the peoples renew their strength" — yachalifu khoach, the words that close the chapter before: those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength (40:31). Here the nations are told to gather what strength they have and come to court.

  • vv2, 25 "one from the east… from the north… one who calls on My name" — the conqueror is not named yet. The book names him at 44:28 and 45:1: Cyrus.

  • v4 "I, the LORD, the first, and with the last, I am He" — ani rishon… ani hu. The words return in 44:6 and 48:12. Revelation gives them to the risen Christ: I am the first and the last (Revelation 1:17; 22:13).

  • vv6–7 "Be strong!… so that it will not totter" — chazaq, the verb the LORD uses of His servant (v9, I took hold of you, hechezaqtikha; v13, hold your right hand, machaziq), here passed from one idol-maker to the next. The idol is nailed down so that it will not totter, as in 40:20.

  • v8 "the offspring of Abraham, My friend" — ohavi, "who loves Me." Jehoshaphat prays in the same words, the seed of Abraham Your friend (2 Chronicles 20:7), and James calls Abraham the friend of God (James 2:23). "Israel, My servant" — avdi, the first time Isaiah calls Israel My servant; Isaiah himself (20:3), Eliakim (22:20) and David (37:35) have had the name before.

  • v14 "your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel" — go'alekh, the first time Isaiah calls the LORD go'el: the next of kin whose duty is to buy back a relative and his land: Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you without a redeemer today (Ruth 4:14). "You worm Jacob" — tola'at, the word of the psalm, I am a worm and not a man (Psalm 22:6).

  • v24 "whoever chooses you is detestable" — to'evah, the law's word for what the LORD will not bear; here it names the one who chooses an idol.

  • vv27–29 "a herald of good news… their metal images are wind and emptiness" — mevasser, as in 40:9. The idols' images are ruach va-tohu: the ruach that is the LORD's Spirit in 40:7 and 13 is here mere wind, and tohu is the word of 40:17, 23, emptiness.

Set forth your case, says the LORD; bring your strong arguments, says the King of Jacob.

But when I look, there is no one; among these there is no counselor who, when I ask, gives an answer.
They are all a delusion; their works are nothing; their metal images are wind and emptiness.

chapters.title: Here Is My Servant
chapters.html:
Isaiah 42

1Here is My servant, whom I uphold,
My chosen one, in whom My soul delights;
I have put My Spirit on him;
he will bring forth justice to the nations.

2He will not cry out or lift up his voice,
or make it heard in the street;

3a crushed reed he will not break,
and a dimly burning wick he will not quench;
he will faithfully bring forth justice.

4He will not grow dim or be crushed
until he has set justice in the earth;
and the coastlands wait for his instruction.

5Thus says God, the LORD,
who created the heavens and stretched them out,
who spread out the earth and what comes from it,
who gives breath to the people on it
and spirit to those who walk in it:

6"I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness;
I will take you by the hand and keep you;
I will give you as a covenant for the people,
a light for the nations,

7to open the eyes that are blind,
to bring out prisoners from the dungeon,
from the prison those who sit in darkness.

8I am the LORD; that is My name;
My glory I give to no other,
nor My praise to carved idols.

9The former things have come to pass,
and new things I now declare;
before they spring up
I tell you of them."

A New Song

10Sing to the LORD a new song,
His praise from the end of the earth,
you who go down to the sea, and all that fills it,
the coastlands and their inhabitants.

11Let the wilderness and its cities lift up their voice,
the villages where Kedar lives;
let the inhabitants of Sela sing for joy;
let them shout from the tops of the mountains.

12Let them give glory to the LORD,
and declare His praise in the coastlands.

13The LORD goes out like a mighty man;
like a man of war He stirs up His zeal;
He shouts, He raises the battle cry;
He shows Himself mighty against His enemies.

14For a long time I have held My peace;
I have kept still and restrained Myself;
now I will cry out like a woman in labor;
I will gasp and pant together.

15I will lay waste mountains and hills,
and dry up all their green growth;
I will turn rivers into dry land,
and dry up the pools.

16I will lead the blind by a way they do not know;
in paths they do not know I will guide them.
I will turn the darkness before them into light,
the rough places into level ground.
These are the things I will do,
and I will not forsake them.

17They will be turned back and utterly put to shame,
those who trust in carved idols,
who say to metal images,
"You are our gods."

The Blind Servant

18Hear, you deaf;
and look, you blind, that you may see!

19Who is blind but My servant,
or deaf like My messenger whom I send?
Who is blind like the one at peace with Me,
or blind like the servant of the LORD?

20You see many things, but do not keep them;
ears are open, but no one hears.

21The LORD was pleased, for the sake of His righteousness,
to make His instruction great and glorious.

22But this is a people plundered and looted;
they are all trapped in holes
and hidden in prisons;
they have become plunder with no one to rescue,
spoil with no one to say, "Give it back!"

23Who among you will give ear to this,
will listen and hear for the time to come?

24Who gave up Jacob to the looter,
and Israel to the plunderers?
Was it not the LORD,
against whom we have sinned,
in whose ways they would not walk,
and whose instruction they did not obey?

25So He poured out on him the heat of His anger
and the fury of battle;
it set him on fire all around, but he did not understand;
it burned him, but he did not take it to heart.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "Here is My servant… a crushed reed he will not break" — Matthew quotes the passage of Jesus, healing quietly and telling the crowds not to make Him known: Here is My servant whom I have chosen, My beloved in whom My soul is well pleased. I will put My Spirit upon Him… A bruised reed He will not break (Matthew 12:18–21). The Greek of Isaiah names the servant: Jacob My servant… Israel My chosen; and in 41:8 and 42:19 the LORD calls Israel My servant.

  • vv3–4 "a crushed reed… a dimly burning wick… He will not grow dim or be crushed" — qaneh ratsuts, the crushed reed the Rabshakeh called Egypt (36:6), which pierces the hand that leans on it. This servant will not break such a reed. And the two words return of the servant himself: lo yikhheh ve-lo yaruts, he will not grow dim (kehah, the wick's word) or be crushed (ratsats, the reed's word).

  • v4 "the coastlands wait for his instruction" — le-torato. The Greek has in his name the nations will hope, and Matthew quotes that (Matthew 12:21).

  • v5 "who spread out the earth" — roqa, the verb behind raqia, the beaten expanse of Genesis 1:6, used of metal hammered flat. "Breath… and spirit" — neshamah and ruach, the breath God blew into his nostrils (Genesis 2:7) given to all who walk the earth.

  • vv6–7 "a light for the nations, to open the eyes that are blind" — Simeon, holding the child in the temple, calls Him a light for revelation to the nations (Luke 2:32). The eyes Isaiah was sent to shut (6:10) are to be opened.

  • v13 "like a man of war" — ke-ish milchamot, as in the Song of the Sea, The LORD is a man of war (Exodus 15:3).

  • v14 "now I will cry out like a woman in labor" — the LORD, silent through the years of judgment, speaks of Himself as a mother in birth pangs, the picture used of the people's own fruitless labor in 26:17–18.

  • vv18–20 "Who is blind but My servant… ears are open, but no one hears" — the servant Israel is blind and deaf, the people of 6:9–10, Keep on listening, but do not understand. "The one at peace with Me" — meshullam, from the root of shalom: one made whole, or bound by a covenant of peace; the sense is uncertain.

  • v22 "plundered and looted… plunder with no one to rescue" — bazuz, baz: the plunder of Maher-shalal-hash-baz (8:1), now taken from Israel.

chapters.title: I Have Called You by Name
chapters.html:
Isaiah 43

1But now, thus says the LORD,
who created you, Jacob,
who formed you, Israel:
"Do not fear, for I have redeemed you;
I have called you by name; you are Mine.

2When you pass through the waters, I will be with you;
and through the rivers, they will not sweep over you;
when you walk through fire, you will not be burned,
and the flame will not consume you.

3For I am the LORD your God,
the Holy One of Israel, your Savior;
I give Egypt as your ransom,
Cush and Seba in your place.

4Because you are precious in My eyes,
and honored, and I love you,
I give men in your place,
and peoples in exchange for your life.

5Do not fear, for I am with you;
I will bring your offspring from the east,
and from the west I will gather you.

6I will say to the north, 'Give them up!'
and to the south, 'Do not hold them back!'
Bring My sons from afar,
and My daughters from the end of the earth,

7everyone who is called by My name,
whom I created for My glory,
whom I formed, yes, whom I made."

8Bring out the people who are blind, yet have eyes,
who are deaf, yet have ears!

9All the nations gather together,
and the peoples assemble.
Who among them can declare this,
and show us the former things?
Let them bring their witnesses to prove them right,
and let others hear and say, "It is true."

10"You are My witnesses," declares the LORD,
"and My servant whom I have chosen,
so that you may know and believe Me
and understand that I am He.
Before Me no god was formed,
nor will there be any after Me.

11I, I am the LORD,
and besides Me there is no savior.

12I declared and saved and proclaimed,
when there was no strange god among you;
and you are My witnesses," declares the LORD,
"and I am God.

13From this day on I am He;
there is no one who can deliver from My hand;
I act, and who can turn it back?"

14Thus says the LORD,
your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel:
"For your sake I have sent to Babylon
and will bring them all down as fugitives,
the Chaldeans, in the ships they rejoiced in.

15I am the LORD, your Holy One,
the Creator of Israel, your King."

16Thus says the LORD,
who makes a way in the sea,
a path in the mighty waters,

17who brings out chariot and horse,
army and warrior;
they lie down together, they cannot rise;
they are extinguished, quenched like a wick:

18"Do not remember the former things,
or consider the things of old.

19I am about to do a new thing;
now it springs up; do you not perceive it?
I will make a way in the wilderness
and rivers in the desert.

20The wild beasts will honor Me,
the jackals and the ostriches,
for I give water in the wilderness,
rivers in the desert,
to give drink to My chosen people,

21the people whom I formed for Myself,
that they might declare My praise.

22Yet you did not call on Me, Jacob;
you have grown weary of Me, Israel.

23You have not brought Me your sheep for burnt offerings,
or honored Me with your sacrifices.
I have not made you serve with offerings,
or wearied you with frankincense.

24You have not bought Me fragrant cane with money,
or satisfied Me with the fat of your sacrifices.
But you have made Me serve with your sins;
you have wearied Me with your iniquities.

25I, I am He
who blots out your transgressions for My own sake,
and I will not remember your sins.

26Remind Me; let us argue our case together;
set forth your case, that you may be proved right.

27Your first father sinned,
and your spokesmen rebelled against Me.

28So I profaned the princes of the sanctuary,
and gave Jacob over to destruction
and Israel to reviling."

Notes

  • vv1, 7, 21 "who created you… who formed you… whom I created… whom I formed… whom I made" — bara, yatsar, asah, the three verbs of the making of the world and of man (Genesis 1:1, 2:7, 1:26), used here of the making of a people.

  • v3 "I give Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba in your place" — kofer, the ransom each Israelite paid for his life when he was counted (Exodus 30:12). Seba is a son of Cush in the table of nations (Genesis 10:7); Cush is the land the Greek calls Ethiopia (18:1 note).

  • vv10, 13, 25 "I am He" — ani hu, as in 41:4. "Before Me no god was formed" — notsar, the verb of v1 and v7: the LORD formed Israel, and before Him no god was formed.

  • v13 "I act, and who can turn it back?" — mi yeshivennah, as in 14:27, His hand is stretched out, and who will turn it back?

  • v17 "quenched like a wick" — kapishtah khavu: the army of Egypt went out like a wick. The servant of 42:3 will not quench even a dimly burning wick (pishtah… lo yekhabbenah).

  • vv19–21 "I am about to do a new thing… the people whom I formed for Myself, that they might declare My praise" — Peter calls the church by the Greek of vv20–21: a chosen race… a people for His own possession, that you may proclaim the excellencies of Him who called you (1 Peter 2:9).

  • vv22–24 "you have grown weary of Me… I have not made you serve… you have made Me serve… you have wearied Me" — yaga and he'evid, turned back on the people: the LORD did not make Israel serve Him or weary them with offerings, but they made Him serve with their sins and wearied Him with their iniquities. The God who does not grow faint or weary (40:28) is wearied by sin. "You have not bought Me fragrant cane" — qanita… qaneh, "bought… cane," two words that sound alike.

  • v25 "who blots out your transgressions" — mocheh, the verb of blot out my transgressions (Psalm 51:1) and of Moses' plea, blot me out, please, from Your book (Exodus 32:32).

  • v28 "gave Jacob over to destruction" — la-cherem, the ban laid on the nations and on Edom (34:2, 5), here laid on Jacob.

chapters.title: Besides Me There Is No God
chapters.html:
Isaiah 44

1But now hear, Jacob My servant,
Israel whom I have chosen.

2Thus says the LORD who made you,
who formed you from the womb and will help you:
"Do not fear, Jacob My servant,
Jeshurun whom I have chosen.

3For I will pour water on the thirsty land,
and streams on the dry ground;
I will pour My Spirit on your seed,
and My blessing on your descendants.

4They will spring up among the grass
like willows by flowing streams.

5One will say, 'I am the LORD's';
another will call himself by the name of Jacob;
another will write on his hand, 'The LORD's,'
and take the name of Israel as a title."

6Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel,
and his Redeemer, the LORD of hosts:
"I am the first and I am the last;
besides Me there is no god.

7Who is like Me? Let him proclaim it;
let him declare it and set it in order before Me,
since I appointed an ancient people.
Let them declare what is to come,
and what will happen.

8Do not tremble, and do not be afraid.
Have I not told you from of old and declared it?
You are My witnesses!
Is there a God besides Me?
There is no Rock; I know of none."

The Idol Maker

9All who form idols are emptiness,
and the things they delight in do not profit;
their witnesses neither see nor know,
so that they will be put to shame.

10Who forms a god or casts an idol
that profits nothing?

11All his companions will be put to shame,
and the craftsmen are only human.
Let them all assemble, let them stand up;
they will be terrified; they will be put to shame together.

12The ironsmith takes a cutting tool
and works it over the coals;
he forms it with hammers
and works it with his strong arm;
he becomes hungry, and his strength fails;
he drinks no water and grows faint.

13The carpenter stretches a line;
he marks it out with a stylus;
he shapes it with planes
and marks it with a compass;
he shapes it into the figure of a man,
with the beauty of a human,
to dwell in a house.

14He cuts down cedars for himself,
or takes a cypress or an oak
and lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest;
he plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.

15Then it becomes fuel for a man;
he takes part of it and warms himself;
he kindles a fire and bakes bread;
he also makes a god and worships it;
he makes it an idol and bows down to it.

16Half of it he burns in the fire;
over that half he eats meat;
he roasts a roast and is satisfied;
he also warms himself and says,
"Aha, I am warm; I see the fire!"

17The rest of it he makes into a god, his idol;
he bows down to it and worships;
he prays to it and says,
"Deliver me, for you are my god!"

18They do not know, nor do they understand;
for their eyes are smeared over so that they cannot see,
and their hearts so that they cannot understand.

19No one stops to think,
nor is there knowledge or understanding to say,
"Half of it I burned in the fire;
I also baked bread on its coals;
I roasted meat and have eaten.
Shall I make the rest of it a detestable thing?
Shall I bow down to a block of wood?"

20He feeds on ashes;
a deluded heart has led him astray,
and he cannot deliver himself or say,
"Is there not a lie in my right hand?"

I Have Redeemed You

21Remember these things, Jacob,
and Israel, for you are My servant;
I formed you; you are My servant;
Israel, you will not be forgotten by Me.

22I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud,
and your sins like mist;
return to Me, for I have redeemed you.

23Sing, you heavens, for the LORD has done it;
shout, you depths of the earth;
break out into singing, you mountains,
you forest, and every tree in it!
For the LORD has redeemed Jacob,
and will be glorified in Israel.

24Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer,
who formed you from the womb:
"I am the LORD, who made all things,
who alone stretched out the heavens,
who spread out the earth by Myself;

25who frustrates the signs of the babblers,
and makes fools of diviners;
who turns wise men back,
and makes their knowledge foolish;

26who confirms the word of His servant,
and fulfills the counsel of His messengers;
who says of Jerusalem, 'She shall be inhabited,'
and of the cities of Judah, 'They shall be built,
and I will raise up their ruins';

27who says to the deep, 'Be dry;
I will dry up your rivers';

28who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd,
and he shall carry out all My purpose,'
saying of Jerusalem, 'She shall be built,'
and of the temple, 'Your foundation shall be laid.'"

Notes

  • v2 "Jeshurun whom I have chosen" — Yeshurun, from yashar, "upright," a name for Israel in the Song and Blessing of Moses: Jeshurun grew fat and kicked (Deuteronomy 32:15); There is none like God, Jeshurun (33:26). The Greek has the beloved Israel.

  • v3 "I will pour My Spirit on your seed" — the promise of 32:15, until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high, here poured on the children.

  • v6 "I am the first and I am the last" — as in 41:4 and 48:12; Revelation 1:17 gives the words to the risen Christ.

  • v8 "There is no Rock; I know of none" — tsur, the name the Song of Moses gives the LORD: The Rock — His work is whole (Deuteronomy 32:4).

  • vv9–10 "All who form idols… Who forms a god" — yotsrei, yatsar, the verb the LORD uses of forming Israel (vv2, 21, 24). In v9 the printed Hebrew has dots set over the word hemmah, "they" (their witnesses, they neither see), a mark of the scribes; the text gives no reason for it.

  • v12 "he grows faint" — va-yi'af, the word of 40:28–31: the LORD does not grow faint or weary; the man who makes a god does.

  • v13 "the figure of a man, with the beauty of a human" — tavnit ish, tif'eret adam: man was made in the likeness of God (Genesis 1:26), and the carpenter makes his god in the likeness of a man.

  • vv15–19 "Half of it he burns… the rest of it he makes into a god" — one log does for the oven, the dinner and the god. "A detestable thing" — to'evah.

  • vv22–24 "blotted out… I have redeemed you… your Redeemer" — machiti, as in 43:25; ge'altikha, go'alekha: the kinsman who buys back (41:14). "By Myself" (v24) — the read form me-itti, "from with Me," is followed; the written form is mi itti, "who was with Me?"

  • v28 "who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd'" — the conqueror of 41:2, 25, named at last. Chronicles and Ezra close and open with his decree: Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: The LORD, the God of heaven… has appointed me to build Him a house in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 36:23; Ezra 1:2).

The carpenter stretches a line; he marks it out with a stylus; he shapes it with planes and marks it with a compass; he shapes it into the figure of a man, with the beauty of a human, to dwell in a house.
He cuts down cedars for himself, or takes a cypress or an oak and lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest; he plants a pine, and the rain makes it grow.
Then it becomes fuel for a man; he takes part of it and warms himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread; he also makes a god and worships it; he makes it an idol and bows down to it.
Half of it he burns in the fire; over that half he eats meat; he roasts a roast and is satisfied; he also warms himself and says, "Aha, I am warm; I see the fire!"
The rest of it he makes into a god, his idol; he bows down to it and worships; he prays to it and says, "Deliver me, for you are my god!"
They do not know, nor do they understand; for their eyes are smeared over so that they cannot see, and their hearts so that they cannot understand.

No one stops to think, nor is there knowledge or understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in the fire; I also baked bread on its coals; I roasted meat and have eaten. Shall I make the rest of it a detestable thing? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?"
He feeds on ashes; a deluded heart has led him astray, and he cannot deliver himself or say, "Is there not a lie in my right hand?"
I Have Redeemed You
Remember these things, Jacob, and Israel, for you are My servant; I formed you; you are My servant; Israel, you will not be forgotten by Me.
I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like mist; return to Me, for I have redeemed you.

Sing, you heavens, for the LORD has done it; shout, you depths of the earth; break out into singing, you mountains, you forest, and every tree in it! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and will be glorified in Israel.
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: "I am the LORD, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by Myself;
who frustrates the signs of the babblers, and makes fools of diviners; who turns wise men back, and makes their knowledge foolish;

who confirms the word of His servant, and fulfills the counsel of His messengers; who says of Jerusalem, 'She shall be inhabited,' and of the cities of Judah, 'They shall be built, and I will raise up their ruins';
who says to the deep, 'Be dry; I will dry up your rivers';
who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd, and he shall carry out all My purpose,' saying of Jerusalem, 'She shall be built,' and of the temple, 'Your foundation shall be laid.'"

chapters.title: To Cyrus, His Anointed
chapters.html:
Isaiah 45

1Thus says the LORD to His anointed,
to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped,
to subdue nations before him
and to loosen the belts of kings,
to open doors before him,
so that gates will not be shut:

2"I will go before you
and level the swelling hills;
I will break in pieces the doors of bronze
and cut through the bars of iron;

3I will give you the treasures of darkness
and the hoards in secret places,
so that you may know that it is I, the LORD,
the God of Israel, who call you by name.

4For the sake of Jacob My servant,
and Israel My chosen,
I call you by your name;
I give you a title of honor,
though you do not know Me.

5I am the LORD, and there is no other;
besides Me there is no God.
I gird you,
though you do not know Me,

6so that they may know,
from the rising of the sun and from the west,
that there is none besides Me;
I am the LORD, and there is no other.

7I form light and create darkness;
I make peace and create disaster;
I am the LORD, who does all these things.

8Drip down, you heavens, from above,
and let the skies rain down righteousness;
let the earth open, that deliverance may bear fruit,
and let it make righteousness sprout up with it;
I, the LORD, have created it.

9Woe to him who strives with the One who formed him,
a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth!
Does the clay say to the one who forms it, 'What are you making?'
or your work say, 'He has no hands'?

10Woe to him who says to a father, 'What are you begetting?'
or to a woman, 'With what are you in labor?'"

11Thus says the LORD,
the Holy One of Israel, and the One who formed him:
"Ask Me about the things to come;
will you command Me concerning My children
and the work of My hands?

12I made the earth
and created man on it;
My hands stretched out the heavens,
and I commanded all their host.

13I have stirred him up in righteousness,
and I will make all his ways level;
he will build My city
and set My exiles free,
not for price or reward,"
says the LORD of hosts.

14Thus says the LORD:
"The labor of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush,
and the Sabeans, men of stature,
will come over to you and be yours;
they will follow you;
they will come over in chains
and bow down to you;
they will plead with you, saying:
'Surely God is in you, and there is no other;
there is no god besides Him.'"

15Truly, You are a God who hides Himself,
the God of Israel, the Savior.

16They are put to shame and disgraced, all of them;
the makers of idols go away together in disgrace.

17But Israel is delivered by the LORD
with an everlasting deliverance;
you will not be put to shame or disgraced
to all eternity.

18For thus says the LORD,
who created the heavens
(He is God!),
who formed the earth and made it
(He established it;
He did not create it to be empty;
He formed it to be inhabited):
"I am the LORD, and there is no other.

19I did not speak in secret,
in a land of darkness;
I did not say to the offspring of Jacob,
'Seek Me in emptiness.'
I, the LORD, speak what is right;
I declare what is upright.

20Assemble yourselves and come;
draw near together, you survivors of the nations!
They have no knowledge,
who carry about their wooden idols
and keep praying to a god that cannot save.

21Declare it and present your case;
let them take counsel together!
Who told this long ago?
Who declared it of old?
Was it not I, the LORD?
There is no other god besides Me,
a righteous God and a Savior;
there is none besides Me.

22Turn to Me and be saved,
all the ends of the earth!
For I am God, and there is no other.

23By Myself I have sworn;
from My mouth has gone out in righteousness
a word that will not return:
'To Me every knee shall bow,
every tongue shall swear.'

24'Only in the LORD,' it shall be said of Me,
'are righteousness and strength.'
To Him shall come and be ashamed
all who were incensed against Him.

25In the LORD all the offspring of Israel
shall be justified and shall glory."

Notes

  • v1 "to His anointed, to Cyrus" — limshicho, mashiach, the title of Israel's kings, the LORD's anointed (1 Samuel 24:6), given here to a king of another nation who does not know the LORD (vv4, 5). The Greek has to My christ Cyrus. "Whose right hand I have grasped" — hechezaqti, the verb of 41:9, 13, used of Israel.

  • vv1, 5 "to loosen the belts of kings… I gird you" — mothnei melakhim afatteach and a'azzerkha: the LORD ungirds the kings Cyrus defeats, and girds Cyrus.

  • v7 "I make peace and create disaster" — ra, the word for evil and for harm, set here against shalom, "peace, welfare." Amos asks the same: If disaster comes to a city, has not the LORD done it? (Amos 3:6, ra'ah).

  • v9 "Woe to him who strives with the One who formed him" — yotsro, the potter, as in 29:16, and the word for the LORD who formed Israel (43:1; 44:2). Paul uses the picture: Will what is formed say to the one who formed it, "Why did you make me like this?" (Romans 9:20).

  • v14 "the merchandise of Cush, and the Sabeans, men of stature" — the land the Greek calls Ethiopia (18:1 note), and Seba (43:3), its people tall, as the nation tall and smooth of 18:2. They come to Zion and say, Surely God is in you.

  • v15 "Truly, You are a God who hides Himself" — El mistatter, as Isaiah waited for the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob (8:17). The God who is hidden is the God who saves.

  • vv18–19 "He did not create it to be empty… Seek Me in emptiness" — tohu, the word rendered wild in Genesis 1:2, the earth was wild and waste. The LORD did not make the earth to stay so, and He did not send Jacob to look for Him there.

  • v23 "To Me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear" — Paul quotes it of God's judgment (every tongue shall confess to God, Romans 14:11), and of Jesus: at the name of Jesus every knee should bow… and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord (Philippians 2:10–11).

  • v25 "shall be justified" — yitsdequ, "be declared righteous," from the root of righteousness in vv8, 13, 19, 21, 23, 24.

chapters.title: Bel Bows Down
chapters.html:
Isaiah 46

1Bel bows down; Nebo stoops;
their idols are on beasts and cattle;
the things you carry are loaded
as a burden on weary beasts.

2They stoop, they bow down together;
they cannot save the burden,
but they themselves go into captivity.

3Listen to Me, house of Jacob,
and all the remnant of the house of Israel,
you who have been loaded on Me from birth,
carried from the womb;

4even to your old age I am He,
and to gray hairs I will bear you.
I have made, and I will carry;
I will bear, and I will save.

5To whom will you liken Me and make Me equal,
and compare Me, that we may be alike?

6Those who lavish gold from the purse,
and weigh out silver on the scale,
hire a goldsmith, and he makes it into a god;
then they fall down and worship!

7They lift it on their shoulders, they bear it;
they set it in its place, and it stands there;
from its place it does not move.
If one cries to it, it does not answer,
or save him from his trouble.

8Remember this and stand firm;
take it to heart, you transgressors.

9Remember the former things of old;
for I am God, and there is no other;
I am God, and there is none like Me,

10declaring the end from the beginning,
and from ancient times things not yet done,
saying, "My counsel shall stand,
and I will do all My purpose,"

11calling a bird of prey from the east,
the man of My counsel from a far country.
I have spoken, and I will bring it to pass;
I have planned it, and I will do it.

12Listen to Me, you stubborn of heart,
you who are far from righteousness:

13I bring near My righteousness; it is not far off,
and My deliverance will not delay;
I will put deliverance in Zion,
for Israel My glory.

Notes

  • v1 "Bel bows down; Nebo stoops" — gods of Babylon. Jeremiah's oracle on Babylon names Bel too: Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed (Jeremiah 50:2).

  • vv1–4, 7 "the things you carry are loaded… you who have been loaded on Me… I will carry… they bear it" — nasa, "carry," amas, "load," and saval, "bear," each said twice: once of the idols, which have to be loaded on animals and borne on men's shoulders, and once of the LORD, who has carried Israel from the womb and will bear them to old age. The idols are a burden; the LORD bears His people. Saval is the verb of the servant who will bear the people's sorrows and iniquities (53:4, 11).

  • v5 "To whom will you liken Me and make Me equal" — tedammeyuni and tashvu, the two verbs of 40:25, To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal? "And compare Me" — tamshiluni, from mashal, added here.

  • v10 "declaring the end from the beginning" — me-reshit acharit; reshit is the word of Genesis 1:1, In the beginning.

  • v11 "a bird of prey from the east, the man of My counsel" — Cyrus, named in 44:28 and 45:1. The read form atsati, "My counsel," is followed.

  • vv12–13 "you who are far from righteousness… it is not far off" — rechoqim, lo tirchaq: the people are far from it; the LORD's righteousness is not far from them.
